extracted.intended_audience: USAMO/JMO contestants, coaches, graders, problem-writers, and contest analysts
extracted.subtask_description: Year-by-year compiled statistics for the USA(J)MO contests, including overall score summaries and per-problem score distributions, plus medal/recognition boundaries and caveats about data quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: N (number of contestants)
rubrics_metrics.description: N — the number of contestants included in the summary for that year (e.g., 'N 294').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported per year for USAMO and JMO; subject to caveats (see data caveats entry) about whether some students were excluded/recorded as zero.

rubrics_metrics.name: µ (mean total score)
rubrics_metrics.description: µ — the mean (average) total score of contestants for the year (e.g., 'µ 9.00').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported per year; gives central tendency of total scores (out of possible 42).

rubrics_metrics.name: σ (standard deviation)
rubrics_metrics.description: σ — the standard deviation of total scores for the year (e.g., 'σ 8.02').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported per year; indicates spread/variability of total scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quartiles (1st Q, Median, 3rd Q)
rubrics_metrics.description: 1st Q, Median, 3rd Q — the first quartile, median, and third quartile of total scores for the year (e.g., '1st Q 3; Median 7; 3rd Q 13').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported per year; useful for understanding distribution skew and central tendency beyond the mean.

rubrics_metrics.name: Max (maximum total score)
rubrics_metrics.description: Max — the maximum total score achieved in that year (e.g., 'Max 42').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported per year; indicates top performance (theoretical maximum is 42 for USAMO/JMO as shown).

rubrics_metrics.name: Top 12 / Top 24 scores
rubrics_metrics.description: Top 12, Top 24 — the minimum scores needed to be among the top 12 or top 24 scorers in that year (e.g., 'Top 12 27; Top 24 21').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported per year as thresholds corresponding to ranking cutoffs used in summaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem labels (AMO1–AMO6, JMO1–JMO6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Problems are labeled AMO1..AMO6 for USAMO and JMO1..JMO6 for JMO; per-problem statistics are reported by these labels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistent labeling used throughout the document for per-problem distributions and metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Per-problem score distribution (counts for scores 0–7)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each problem the document lists counts of contestants receiving each integer score 0,1,2,...,7 (displayed as a histogram of counts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These per-score counts are the core per-problem distribution data (used to compute Avg, QM, #5+, %5+). Examples with raw counts are provided for every problem/year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem Avg (average problem score)
rubrics_metrics.description: Avg — the average score on that problem across contestants (e.g., 'Avg 2.66').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported alongside per-problem distributions; shows mean difficulty (lower Avg = harder problem on average).

rubrics_metrics.name: QM (reported per-problem secondary metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: QM — an additional per-problem metric reported in the tables (values shown, e.g., 'QM 4.12'), presented without an explicit definition on the page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document reports QM alongside Avg; the page does not define QM explicitly, so users should treat it as a provided statistic (likely a spread/quality measure) but consult source if precise definition is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: #5+ (count scoring 5 or more)
rubrics_metrics.description: #5+ — the number of contestants who scored 5 or greater on that problem (e.g., '#5+ 104').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported per problem/year; useful as a measure of how many contestants solved or nearly solved the problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: %5+ (percentage scoring 5 or more)
rubrics_metrics.description: %5+ — the percent of contestants scoring 5 or greater on that problem (e.g., '%5+ %35.4').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported per problem/year; gives a normalized measure of how commonly high scores occurred on that problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medal/recognition system (post-2022 change)
rubrics_metrics.description: Starting in 2022 the USAMO and JMO switched to a medal/recognition system: USAMO contestants may receive gold, silver, or bronze medals; JMO contestants may receive 'top honors' or 'honors'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The document explains the system change and reports per-year minimum scores for each medal/recognition (see per-year tables).

rubrics_metrics.name: Medal allocation percentages (approximate)
rubrics_metrics.description: USAMO medals are given to approximately 6% (gold), 12% (silver), and 18% (bronze) of contestants. About 20% of JMO contestants receive 'top honors' or 'honors' status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These percentages are approximate guidelines for how many medals/recognitions are awarded each year under the new system (starting 2022).

rubrics_metrics.name: Honorable mention threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Anyone earning 14 points or more obtains an honorable mention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as a fixed points threshold for honorable mentions under the described awards system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Per-year minimum score tables for medals/recognitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables listing the minimum score needed for each medal/recognition by year (e.g., USAMO 2026: Gold 25, Silver 18, Bronze 11; similar tables for 2022–2026 and JMO thresholds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides historical thresholds; useful for benchmarking performance and tracking year-to-year variation in award cutoffs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data caveats and sources of discrepancy
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit caveats about data quality: students who do not take the exam may be recorded as zero or omitted; students taking only one day; students taking the wrong exam; mislabelled ID/problem numbers; inconsistent inclusion of non‑US/Canadian students; grader/compiler mistakes; and other edge cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author states figures should be seen as rough estimates for educational reference only and not as authoritative official data; use caution when interpreting small differences or exact counts.
